words.tip: 你好 (nǐ hǎo) = “you good”. Two 3rd tones in a row: the first becomes 2nd tone, so it sounds like ní hǎo.
In Taiwan people say 早安 (zǎo'ān) or just 早 (zǎo)! 早上好 (zǎoshang hǎo) sounds more mainland.
Friends in Taiwan also just say 掰掰 (bāibāi), from “bye-bye”!
好 (hǎo) = 女 (nǚ, woman) + 子 (zǐ, child) → “good”.
謝謝 (xièxie): the second 謝 (xie) is light and short: “shyeh-shyeh”.
In Taiwan 氣 (qì) keeps its 4th tone: bú kèqì.
不好意思 (bù hǎoyìsi) is the super-common Taiwan “excuse me / sorry to bother you”.

words.z: ㄏㄣˇ ㄍㄠ ㄒㄧㄥˋ ㄖㄣˋ ㄕˋ ㄋㄧˇ

words.tip: 四 (sì) sounds like 死 (sǐ, death), so 4 is an unlucky number. Many buildings in Taiwan skip the 4th floor!
八 (bā) sounds like 發 (fā, get rich): a lucky number! 🍀

words.tip: 水 (shuǐ) looks like a stream with splashes on both sides 💧.
In Taiwan a bowl of plain rice is 白飯 (báifàn, “white rice”).
At Taiwanese restaurants you order “a plate of 青菜 (qīngcài)” (greens).
起司 (qǐsī) comes from the English word “cheese”!
Careful: in Taiwan 土豆 (tǔdòu) means peanut, not potato! 🥜
Invented in Taiwan! 珍珠 (zhēnzhū) = pearls. Order 半糖 (bàn táng) for half sugar. 🧋
紅 (hóng) is the color of luck: red envelopes, 紅包 (hóngbāo) 🧧!
Taiwan says 橘色 (júsè, tangerine color) for orange.
Brown in Taiwan is 咖啡色 (kāfēisè): literally “coffee color” ☕.
媽 (mā) = 女 (nǚ, woman) + 馬 (mǎ, horse, gives the “ma” sound).
Taiwan writes 姊姊 (jiějie); you may also see 姐姐 (jiějie).
奶奶 (nǎinai) is dad's mom. Mom's mom is 外婆 (wàipó).
For “yes / right” Taiwan speakers usually say 對 (duì) or 對啊 (duì a).

words.z: ㄒㄧˇ ㄕㄡˇ ㄐㄧㄢ ㄗㄞˋ ㄋㄚˇ ㄌㄧˇ?

words.tip: 好好吃 (hǎo hǎochī, “so yummy!”) is how you hype food in Taiwan.
Mainland says 出租车 (chūzūchē); Taiwan says 計程車 (jìchéngchē, “meter car”).
捷運 (jiéyùn) is the MRT in Taipei and Kaohsiung. Mainland says 地铁 (dìtiě).
腳踏車 (jiǎotàchē) = “foot-pedal car”. Rent a YouBike in Taiwan! 🚲
In Taiwan 垃圾 (lèsè) is read lèsè (mainland: lājī). Trash trucks there play Für Elise! 🎶

topics.note: Mandarin verbs don't change. Add 了 (le) after the verb for a finished action: 我吃了 (wǒ chī le) = I ate. Time words like 昨天 (zuótiān) go before the verb.

topics.note: Use 會 (huì) = will, or 要 (yào) = going to: 我會去 (wǒ huì qù) = I will go. Time words like 明天 (míngtiān) make the future clear.

topics.name: Grammar: Questions
topics.note: Add 嗎 (ma) to make a yes/no question: 你好嗎？(nǐ hǎo ma?). With question words like 什麼 (shénme) or 哪裡 (nǎlǐ), don't add 嗎 (ma).
